grades.quote: C.BEQZ performs conditional control transfers. The offset is sign-extended and added to the `pc` to form the branch target address.
grades.reason: RISC-V C.BEQZ, which expands to a beq, takes its target as the sign-extended offset added to the pc. This is the compressed form, not the base BEQ, and it is limited to a ±256 B range. The address calculation carries over to BEQ, so it is useful but indirect.

It is only an encoding listing for the compressed C.BEQZ/C.BNEZ instructions. It shows the scattered offset bit fields but does not say how the destination address is computed, and it does not cover BEQ itself.
This is a LoongArch table of contents listing branch instruction names. It is the wrong ISA and has no address calculation.
This describes LoongArch floating-point branches (BCEQZ/BCNEZ). The query requires RISC-V BEQ, so the passage is the wrong ISA.
